card.summary: Native-768 SD2 model; niche today but works perfectly on ComfyUI (auto v-prediction). Its distinct older aesthetic suits heavily stylized art, intentionally low-fi/poor-quality looks, and horror (SFW only).
card.pick_when: Native-768 SFW or an SD2-specific need.

prompt.guidance: Descriptive English; a solid negative helps.
prompt.example: a highly detailed matte painting of a futuristic city at sunset, volumetric light
prompt.overview: OpenCLIP-ViT/H model, 768 native: comma-separated keyword/descriptor tags; well-chosen negative prompts are especially important for quality.
prompt.instructions: Generate at 768x768 (native). Use comma-separated descriptor/quality tags as in the SD1/SDXL era. Guidance scale ~7-9 (default 7.5, range 1-20). Because the OpenCLIP-ViT/H encoder responds differently than SD1.5's CLIP-L, negative prompts are an emphasized lever -- SD2.x typically needs a good negative prompt to reach strong output and anatomy.
do: Always pair with a quality/anatomy negative prompt
dont: Omit a negative prompt (SD2.x relies on it)
examples: a high quality photograph of an astronaut riding a horse, detailed, sharp focus, 8k
portrait of a fox in a forest, golden hour, bokeh, highly detailed
prompt.negative_guidance: Important for SD2.x. Typical: 'blurry, lowres, bad anatomy, bad hands, extra fingers, deformed, watermark, text, jpeg artifacts, ugly'.

speed.measured_note: ~8s for the first image at default settings (768x768, 25 steps, cold: includes model load); repeats with the same model are faster.

ui_help.note: Describe what you want in a sentence or two, like you'd tell ChatGPT. More detail usually looks better. Also good for heavily stylized art, intentionally rough/low-fi looks, and horror (SFW).
ui_help.good_for: classic 768px scenes, heavily stylized art, low-fi/gritty looks, and horror (SFW)
